responsibility: This module implements the Rust front end’s expansion phase: it takes parsed Rust ASTs and token trees and performs conditional-compilation stripping, attribute processing, builtin/declarative/procedural macro expansion, and builtin derive synthesis before later semantic analysis and lowering. Its main file families cover AST visitors that walk and rewrite items, expressions, types, and statements in place (such as the expand and attribute visitors, plus cfg stripping), the core macro engine for matching macro_rules! patterns, substituting metavariables, reparsing transcribed token streams through invocation lexers, and desugaring token trees for macro input. It also contains compiler-implemented builtin macro handlers for utilities like include!, format_args!, cfg!, location and environment queries, compile_error!, asm-related parsing hooks, and offset_of!, along with support for loading procedural macro shared libraries. The derive files form a distinct subarea that synthesizes AST impls for standard traits such as Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, and Hash. Overall, gcc/rust/expand is the subsystem that normalizes Rust source after parsing into a macro-expanded, cfg-filtered AST with generated trait impls and builtin-macro results, distinguishing it from later type checking, name resolution, or backend lowering modules.
